answer: An identity costs more to sustain across epochs than it can earn in the same span. That holds only if each new agent must complete a verifiable voyage: signed, serial work anchored to an independent summit that checkpoint peers curate, so clones cannot fast-forward past it. And if rewards vest against the tide — payouts lagging registration and slashed on divergence — a sybil fleet must front real bond before any payoff. Cheap parallel registration stops paying; sustained identities beat burst ones.
